title: Week summaries in time report
description:
## Overview

Append a weekly day-by-day summary section at the end of the time report. The summary covers Monday through Friday of the current week.

## Tag semantics (relevant to this feature)

| Tag(s) | Meaning | At-work boundary | Counts as worked |
|--------|---------|-----------------|-----------------|
| #per, #personal | Planned personal time — not at work | Stripped from start/end | No |
| #break | Short recharge break during the work day | Not stripped (counts as at work) | No |
| #off-task | Unplanned non-work, not a break | Not stripped (counts as at work) | No |
| Everything else | Work time | Not stripped | Yes |

## Work day boundary calculation

1. Walk the day's time log entries in order.
2. Strip any leading #personal/#per blocks from the beginning of the day.
3. Strip any trailing #personal/#per blocks from the end of the day.
4. The remaining window defines the work day: **time tracked start → time tracked end**.
5. #break and #off-task blocks inside the window do NOT break or shrink the boundary.

## Per-day fields

- **time tracked**: start and end timestamps of the work window (HH:MM – HH:MM)
- **total time**: wall-clock duration of the work window (end – start)
- **hours worked**: sum of all entries inside the work window that are NOT #personal, #per, #break, or #off-task

## Report format

Rendered as a markdown indented list at the end of the time report:

```
- 2026-02-16 Mon
  * time tracked:   08:20 - 17:00
  * hours worked:   7 hr 46 min
  * total time:     8 hr 40 min
- 2026-02-17 Tue
  * time tracked:   09:00 - 17:30
  * hours worked:   6 hr 15 min
  * total time:     8 hr 30 min
- 2026-02-18 Wed
  * (no data)
- 2026-02-19 Thu
  * (no data)
- 2026-02-20 Fri
  * (no data)

Weekly total worked: 14 hr 01 min
```

Days with no time log entries show `* (no data)` and are excluded from the weekly total.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Week summary appears at the end of the time report
- Days run Monday–Friday; all five days are always shown
- #personal/#per blocks at the start/end of the day are excluded from the work window boundary
- #break and #off-task blocks inside the window are included in total time but excluded from hours worked
- Days with no data show `* (no data)`
- Weekly total is the sum of hours worked across all days with data
- Tests cover: normal day, day starting/ending with #personal, day with #break mid-day, day with #off-task, empty day
close_reason: Added analyze_work_day, format_week_summary, format_duration_long to time_tracking.py; integrated week summary into time_report.py; added tests

title: Implement advanced tag type tracking
description:
## Overview

The current implementation has two tag types, SPECIAL and ACTIVITY, which are conceptually unclear and should be removed entirely. Replace them with a hardcoded system of named tag groups, and update time reports to present tag data in two sections.

## Remove SPECIAL and ACTIVITY

Remove the SPECIAL and ACTIVITY tag type distinctions from the codebase. All tags are plain tags; grouping is handled separately by the group definitions below.

## Hardcoded Tag Groups

Define the following groups in code:

| Group name | Tags |
|------------|------|
| Meeting    | #mtg, #meeting |
| Personal   | #per, #personal, #off-task |
| Break      | #break |

Rules:
- If a time log entry contains multiple tags from the same group, count it only once for that group (no double-counting).
- Tags may belong to only one group.

## Report Format

Time reports should include two sections:

### 1. Group summary
Show cumulative time per group. Only groups with nonzero time are shown.

Example:
```
Meeting:  2h 30m
Personal: 1h 15m
Break:    45m
```

### 2. Flat tag list
Show every tag that appears in the time log with its individual cumulative time, regardless of group membership.

Example:
```
#break:      45m
#meeting:    1h 30m
#mtg:        1h
#off-task:   30m
#personal:   45m
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- SPECIAL and ACTIVITY tag type concepts are gone from code and tests
- Group totals correctly merge aliases (e.g. #mtg + #meeting entries sum into Meeting)
- Duplicate tags within a single entry are treated as one occurrence
- Flat tag list shows all tags with individual totals
- Existing tests updated; new tests cover group merging and the flat list

title: Implement MetaNotesDaily command
description:
Open/create today's daily note or specific date if provided as [YYYY-MM-DD]

## Requirements

Command: `:MetaNotesDaily [YYYY-MM-DD]`
- Opens today's daily note by default
- Accepts optional date parameter for specific dates
- File path format: `resource/daily-notes/YY-QQQ/YYYY-mm-dd ddd.md`
  - Example: `resource/daily-notes/26-Q1/2026-02-13 Thu.md`
  - YY = two-digit year (26)
  - QQQ = quarter (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4)  
  - YYYY-mm-dd = full date (2026-02-13)
  - ddd = three-letter day abbreviation (Thu)

## Existing Implementation to Reference

- `meta_notes#notes#OpenWeekPlan()` function in `autoload/meta_notes/notes.vim:156-173`
- Already has week start/end calculation functions
- Has pattern for creating directories and adding header templates

## Related Files

- `/Volumes/Data/work/meta-notes/plugin/meta_notes.vim` - Add command definition
- `/Volumes/Data/work/meta-notes/autoload/meta_notes/notes.vim` - Add implementation function
- Will need new test file: `/Volumes/Data/work/meta-notes/test/daily_note.vader`

## Technical Requirements

- Calculate quarter from date (Q1: Jan-Mar, Q2: Apr-Jun, Q3: Jul-Sep, Q4: Oct-Dec)
- Format date with three-letter day abbreviation
- Create nested directory structure if needed
- Apply daily note template (when templates are implemented)
- For now: create basic header like week plan does

## Why This Task First?

1. **Builds on existing patterns** - MetaNotesWeekPlan is already implemented and serves as a great template
2. **Core workflow feature** - Daily notes are the primary interaction point for users
3. **Already partially done** - MetaNotesOpen (che.1) and MetaNotesWeekPlan (che.3) are already working
4. **Enables testing of other features** - Once daily notes work, we can test templates, task finding, time tracking, etc.
5. **Unblocks navigation** - Daily prev/next commands depend on this
6. **Foundation for linking hierarchy** - Daily notes link to weekly plans (already implemented)
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Jonathan Branam
comments.text: Requirements have conflicting statements: 'Weekly plan ↔ Quarterly plan (bidirectional)' but also 'Quarterly plans do NOT link to individual weeks'. How can it be bidirectional if quarterly doesn't link to weeks? Also, yearly template needs to add links to quarterly plans (currently has sections but no wiki-links). Clarify: should quarterly have a list of week links or not?

comments.author: Jonathan Branam
comments.text:
Every standard note template links up to a higher level. Therefore:
daily -> weekly
weekly -> quarterly
quarterly -> yearly

The yearly plan also links to the quarterly plans. Weeks DO NOT link to days, quarters DO NOT link to weeks.
